quotes.quote: In war, we are one people. In making peace, we are one people. In all commercial regulations, we are one and the same people. In many other respects, the American people are one; and the government which is alone capable of controlling and managing their interests in all these respects, is the government of the Union.
quotes.author: John Marshall
quotes.headline: In War, One People
quotes.source: John Marshall, Cohens v. Virginia (1821)
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against the opinion text on Cornell LII, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: The art of war is of vital importance to the State. It is a matter of life and death, a road either to safety or to ruin. Hence it is a subject of inquiry which can on no account be neglected.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Matter of Life and Death
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. I
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: All warfare is based on deception. Hence, when able to attack, we must seem unable; when using our forces, we must seem inactive; when we are near, we must make the enemy believe we are far away; when far away, we must make him believe we are near.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: All Warfare Is Based on Deception
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. I
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: If his forces are united, separate them. Attack him where he is unprepared, appear where you are not expected.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Attack Him Where He Is Unprepared
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. I
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: There is no instance of a country having benefited from prolonged warfare. It is only one who is thoroughly acquainted with the evils of war that can thoroughly understand the profitable way of carrying it on.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: No Country Benefits From Prolonged War
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. II
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: In war, then, let your great object be victory, not lengthy campaigns. Thus it may be known that the leader of armies is the arbiter of the people’s fate, the man on whom it depends whether the nation shall be in peace or in peril.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Victory, Not Lengthy Campaigns
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. II
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Hence to fight and conquer in all your battles is not supreme excellence; supreme excellence consists in breaking the enemy’s resistance without fighting.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Supreme Excellence Against Adversaries
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. III
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Thus the highest form of generalship is to baulk the enemy’s plans; the next best is to prevent the junction of the enemy’s forces; the next in order is to attack the enemy’s army in the field; and the worst policy of all is to besiege walled cities.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Highest Form of Generalship
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. III
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Hence the saying: If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles. If you know yourself but not the enemy, for every victory gained you will also suffer a defeat. If you know neither the enemy nor yourself, you will succumb in every battle.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Know the Enemy and Know Yourself
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. III
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: He will win who knows when to fight and when not to fight.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Know When to Fight
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. III
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: The good fighters of old first put themselves beyond the possibility of defeat, and then waited for an opportunity of defeating the enemy. To secure ourselves against defeat lies in our own hands, but the opportunity of defeating the enemy is provided by the enemy himself.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: First, Beyond the Possibility of Defeat
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. IV
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Thus it is that in war the victorious strategist only seeks battle after the victory has been won, whereas he who is destined to defeat first fights and afterwards looks for victory.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Win First, Then Fight
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. IV
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Appear at points which the enemy must hasten to defend; march swiftly to places where you are not expected.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: March Where You Are Not Expected
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. VI
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Water shapes its course according to the nature of the ground over which it flows; the soldier works out his victory in relation to the foe whom he is facing. Therefore, just as water retains no constant shape, so in warfare there are no constant conditions.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: In Warfare, No Constant Conditions
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. VI
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Let your plans be dark and impenetrable as night, and when you move, fall like a thunderbolt.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Fall Like a Thunderbolt
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. VII
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: When you surround an army, leave an outlet free. Do not press a desperate foe too hard.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Leave an Outlet Free
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. VII
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Regard your soldiers as your children, and they will follow you into the deepest valleys; look on them as your own beloved sons, and they will stand by you even unto death.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Stand by You Even Unto Death
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. X
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Throw your soldiers into positions whence there is no escape, and they will prefer death to flight. If they will face death, there is nothing they may not achieve.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Prefer Death to Flight
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. XI
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Move not unless you see an advantage; use not your troops unless there is something to be gained; fight not unless the position is critical. No ruler should put troops into the field merely to gratify his own spleen; no general should fight a battle simply out of pique.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Never Fight Out of Pique
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. XII
quotes.verified_note: checked verbatim against Project Gutenberg #132 (Giles, 1910); commentators' bracketed notes omitted, Oct 16 2026

quotes.quote: Anger may in time change to gladness; vexation may be succeeded by content. But a kingdom that has once been destroyed can never come again into being; nor can the dead ever be brought back to life.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.work: The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles)
quotes.headline: Kingdom Destroyed Can Never Come Again
quotes.source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War (trans. Lionel Giles), ch. XII
